title: John Chrysostom on 2 Corinthians 1:1
body: “Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Timothy our brother, unto the Church of God, which is at Corinth, with all the saints which are in the whole of Achaia: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 1

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Corinthians 1:6
body: “Whether we be afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation, which worketh in the patient enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer: and our hope for you is steadfast.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 2

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Corinthians 2:12
body: “Now when I came to Troas for the gospel of Christ, and when a door was opened unto me in the Lord, I had no relief for my spirit, because I found not Titus my brother.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 5

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Corinthians 3:7
body: “But if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, came with glory, so that the children of Israel could not look steadfastly upon the face of Moses, for the glory of his face; which glory was passing away: how shall not rather the ministration of the Spirit be with glory?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 7

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Corinthians 4:1
body: “Therefore seeing we have this ministry, even as we obtained mercy we faint not, but we have renounced the hidden things of shame.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 8

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Corinthians 4:8
body: “We are pressed on every side, yet not straitened; perplexed, yet not unto despair; pursued, yet not forsaken.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 9

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Corinthians 6:1
body: “And working together with Him we intreat also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain. For he saith, At an acceptable time I hearkened unto thee.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 12

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Corinthians 6:11
body: “Our mouth is open unto you, O ye Corinthians, our heart is enlarged, ye are not straitened in us, but ye are straitened in your own affections.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 13

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Corinthians 10:1
body: “Now I Paul myself entreat you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ, I who in your presence am lowly among you, but being absent am of good courage toward you: yea, I beseech you, that I may not when present show courage with the confidence, wherewith I count to be bold against some, which count of us as if we walked according to the flesh.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 21

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Corinthians 10:7
body: “Ye look at the things that are before your face. If any man trusteth in himself that he is Christ's, let him consider this again with himself that even as he is Christ's, so also are we.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 22

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Corinthians 12:16
body: “But be it so, I myself did not burden you: but being crafty, I caught you with guile. Did I take advantage of you by any one of them whom I have sent unto you?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 28

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Corinthians 13:10
body: “For this cause I write these things while absent, that I may not when present deal sharply, according to the authority which the Lord gave me for building up, and not for casting down.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians, Homily 30
